findings.title: Refresh cache status after successful deletion
findings.body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional callback; it never invalidates or updates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes its optional onChanged callback directly through and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Without a callback that explicitly refetches, deleting the cache therefore leaves the old timestamp and delete action visible after the success toast. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve backing cache records for delegated connections
findings.body: When a connected calendar uses an in-memory delegation credential, its negative credential ID cannot match CalendarCache rows stored against database credentials. The existing getCachedAvailability implementation explicitly handles this case using userId and the cache key, but this status lookup only uses the displayed credential ID. Consequently, a delegated connection can serve cached availability while reporting cacheUpdatedAt as null. Because the duplicate non-delegated connection is filtered out and delegated connections cannot disconnect, the dropdown then disappears entirely, preventing these users from viewing or clearing their cache. Resolve the backing cache records for delegated connections and use that same authorized scope for deletion.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to ../.env outside the repository, potentially creating that file, while leaving the application's configuration unchanged. Derive the repository environment-file path from BASH_SOURCE so the normal root-level invocation updates the intended file.

findings.title: Use an environment-file replacement compatible with GNU sed
findings.body: The sed -i '' syntax is BSD-specific. On Linux with GNU sed, the empty argument is treated as the sed program and the replacement expression as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not updated. The script nevertheless prints its success message, leaving webhook registration pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement or select the appropriate in-place syntax for the installed sed.
